title: Autofluorescence Microscopy Data Acquisition
author: Elizabeth Neumann
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7e3hjgn
materials: Define the imaging region that includes the tissue.

steps.title: Thaw frozen tissue (if needed)
steps.instruction: If the sectioned tissue is frozen, return it to room temperature (~20 °C) inside a vacuum desiccator for approximately 30 minutes; if not frozen, skip this step and continue.

steps.title: Load slide into scanner
steps.instruction: Place the microscope slide within its adapter and insert the assembly into the Zeiss AxioScan Slide Scanner.

steps.title: Coarse focus with DAPI
steps.instruction: Perform coarse focusing of the tissue using the DAPI filter set (excitation 335‑383 nm, emission 420‑470 nm, blue), set lamp power to ~90 % and use a moderate exposure time of ~150 ms.

steps.title: Fine focus and build map
steps.instruction: Perform fine focusing to build a focus map using DAPI (blue), GFP (excitation 450‑490 nm, emission 500‑550 nm, green) and DsRed (excitation 538‑562 nm, emission 570‑640 nm, red) channels, with lamp power ~90 % and exposure ~150 ms for each channel.

steps.title: Export image as OME‑TIF
steps.instruction: Export the autofluorescence image as an OME‑TIF file using the options: “BigTIFF”, “Use Tiles”, “Compress”, and “Convert to 8 Bit”. Alternative file types such as BigTIFF or PNGs may also be used depending on the application.
